architecture.mechanism: Carbon-based microwave susceptors (activated carbon, biochar, coke, graphite) absorb microwave energy and convert it into localized heat via dielectric loss, with absorption efficiency governed by the susceptor's surface area and porosity — enabling targeted heating of specific zones without modifying the bulk cavity field.
architecture.intervention: Embed a food-safe carbon-based susceptor (e.g., a graphite/carbon-impregnated food-grade center "core rod," skewer, or susceptor-lined center plate) into the cold center zone of the food so microwave energy that normally passes unabsorbed through the center is captured and converted to heat exactly at the cold spot, evening out the radial temperature profile without stirring or user intervention.
architecture.expected_effect: Preferential susceptor heating of the cold center reduces the center-to-edge temperature gradient, producing substantially more even heating across the food while the cycle runs unattended.
architecture.falsification_test: Heat a standardized load (food-simulant gel disc) with and without the susceptor insert in the same oven; map temperature with an infrared camera or thermocarbonate grid across at least 5 trials; falsify if the maximum center-to-edge temperature difference is not reduced by 30% or more with the susceptor present.

challenge.kill_reason: all checks passed: evidence verified, no specific disclosure, adversarial survived, falsification concrete
